authority: docs/PAGE_RELEASE_LAW.md and data/strategy/page_strategy_registry.json remain the publishing authority. This file declares only the join between measured query demand and the release queue.
why: The query atlas was read by nobody. Release queue rows all carried source=twin_agent_artifact, and Velocity Content Release only triggered when a human pushed an agent-run manifest - 5 runs and 8 pages since June. Measured demand existed the whole time and could not reach publishing. This contract is the declared, reviewable edge between the two.

admission_rules.why_required: The atlas ranks unmeasured rows with a neutral factor so ordering is not distorted by a number nobody took. Ranking is not admission: a query may only become a page candidate once its citation occupancy has actually been measured. This is the gate that replaced the hardcoded 0.5 weak_incumbent_score, which admitted and blocked nothing.
admission_rules.minimum_citation_occupancy_why: unbranded_share is the fraction of answer-engine citation slots an independent page could plausibly take. Below this, the slots are held by national brands, social surfaces or our own pages, and a new page is competing for something that is not open.
admission_rules.maximum_candidates_per_run_why: A processing budget, never a publication quota. The same principle page_strategy_registry.json states for daily cadence.

route_shape.why: New query pages belong on the Velocity site under an existing governed vertical prefix. The join never invents a vertical: a query that matches no vertical's topic terms, or matches more than one equally, is HELD with a reason rather than routed by guess.

vertical_source_records._why: Every admitted page must carry source records that exist in data/evidence/source_registry.json, or validate_evidence_registry.js fails the build. This is the single authority for the per-vertical defaults; scripts/velocity_content_release.js and scripts/queries/join_atlas_to_release_queue.mjs both read it rather than each keeping a copy.
